meta.case: NorthStar Retail — Reversing the Margin Decline

slides.title: NorthStar should reprice its premium tier and cut low-margin SKUs to recover 4.2 margin points within 18 months
slides.recommendation: Reprice the premium tier (+8%) and rationalize the bottom-quartile SKUs, funded by the freed working capital.
reasons: The premium tier is underpriced vs willingness-to-pay, leaving 8% on the table
The bottom 22% of SKUs generate 3% of profit but 40% of complexity cost
The move pays back in 2.3 years at a 24% ROI with low execution risk
slides.impact: +4.2 operating-margin points · +$96M annual operating profit · 2.3-yr payback

slides.title: Operating margin has fallen 5.1 points in three years despite flat revenue — a pricing and mix problem, not a demand problem
slides.body: Revenue held at ~$2.1B while operating margin slid from 11.8% to 6.7%. The decision: where to intervene to restore margin without eroding the brand.
bullets: Volume stable — the erosion is price and mix

slides.title: The premium tier sells 12% below customer willingness-to-pay, the single largest recoverable margin pool
slides.chart_note: [chart] WTP vs current price by tier — premium gap = 12%
bullets: Conjoint-style benchmark shows premium WTP 12% above list
Premium is 28% of revenue, 46% of gross profit
An 8% increase captures most of the gap with minimal churn

slides.title: The bottom 22% of SKUs earn 3% of profit but drive 40% of supply-chain complexity cost
slides.chart_note: [chart] Profit vs complexity cost by SKU decile — long tail
bullets: Long-tail SKUs: 3% of profit, 40% of complexity cost
Freed capital funds the repricing rollout

slides.title: The combined move adds $96M in annual operating profit and pays back in 2.3 years at a 24% ROI
slides.source: Team financial model; assumptions in appendix A-3

slides.title: Execute in three phases over 18 months, front-loading the SKU cut to fund repricing

phases.label: Months 9–18
phases.text: National rollout; monitor churn and mix

slides.title: The main risks are premium churn and channel pushback, both mitigable with a phased, monitored rollout

risks.mitigation: Regional pilot with churn tripwire before national rollout

risks.risk: Channel partner pushback on delisting SKUs
risks.mitigation: Joint margin-share plan; phase out over two quarters
Sensitivity holds to -6% adoption; hedge key inputs
